history.dynasty: Hoysala (early 12th century rise); patronage by Vijayanagara and the Wodeyars of Mysore
history.period: Over 1000 years old; rose to prominence in the early 12th century with Ramanujacharya's 12-year stay
history.summary: One of the most revered Sri Vaishnava shrines in Karnataka, dedicated to Vishnu as Cheluvanarayana (Tirunarayana). Over 1000 years old, it rose to prominence under Sri Ramanujacharya, who stayed at Melkote for 12 years in the early 12th century and made it the centre of Sri Vaishnavism; per legend he recovered the temple's lost metallic processional idol, Sampath Kumara (Selva Pillai). It was lavishly patronized by the Wodeyars of Mysore - Raja Wodeyar was a great devotee (his bas relief is on a navaranga column) and gifted the Vairamudi (Vajramukuta) and Krishnaraja-mudi crowns. The crowns are kept in government (Mandya district treasury) custody and brought to the temple under armed escort for the annual Vairamudi festival, when the chief priest fits the diamond crown on the deity while blindfolded - tradition holds that no one may see the crown before it adorns Tirunarayana. Dravidian style with Hoysala and Vijayanagara influences; the complex includes the large stepped Kalyani theertha tank and the Akka-Tangi kola sister ponds.

name: Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple
town_description: Melkote (Melukote) is a temple town in Pandavapura taluk of Mandya district, Karnataka, built on the rocky Yadugiri hills overlooking the Cauvery valley, about 51 km from Mysuru and 133 km from Bengaluru. It is one of the most sacred places in Karnataka, home to the Academy of Sanskrit Research with thousands of manuscripts, and a major centre of the Sri Vaishnava tradition ever since Ramanujacharya stayed here for 12 years in the early 12th century.

travel.road: Melkote is ~51 km from Mysuru and ~133 km from Bengaluru; connected by road via Pandavapura.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; visit during Vairamudi Brahmotsava (March-April) for the grand festival
